entry.title: A missing version broke verification of signed ARD search results
entry.summary: Follow an ARD catalog from a domain to a capability, including the signed-result bug and the draft's compatibility limits.

entry.title: A privacy warning became bad advice in an AI reviewer's draft
entry.summary: An adapter dropped WARDEN's advisory flag. A welcome draft then asked a seller to reword a useful privacy warning.

entry.title: Healthy containers hid a blocked MCP marketplace connection
entry.summary: Changing prices rewrote pinned MCP tool definitions. Three assistants lost hub tools while their containers stayed healthy.

entry.title: An MCP tool set can gain a digest without changing
entry.summary: An old refusal can outlive the rules that produced it. MTL labels now record why a tool-set digest is absent and which revision decided it.

entry.title: 242,072 malware flags on npm and PyPI, and what the registries did about them
entry.summary: We measured what open package-malware feeds flag on npm and PyPI, what the registries did, how many flags left up are wrong, and what open scanners cost in false alarms.

entry.title: We found 331 MCP tool-list changes in one week that only moved a date. Each one costs a prompt-cache write
entry.summary: Of 10,712 tool-definition changes HISTOR recorded in a week, 331 changed nothing but a date or a timestamp. Where those dates come from, and where they belong instead.

entry.title: We read the robots.txt of 2,347 MCP hosts: Python 3.12's parser gets 252 endpoints wrong
entry.summary: urllib.robotparser took the first matching rule and read * and $ literally until 2026. Python 3.14.5 and 3.13.14 fixed it; 3.12 never will. On MCP endpoints the difference is 14%.

entry.title: We stopped reading 2,195 MCP servers for three days. Another team's log is how we found out
entry.summary: Our MCP crawler tried the 2026-07-28 protocol first and refused to fall back. Per-read success stayed at 99%. A second, independent log showed what we were missing.

entry.title: An honest x402 seller earned $0.18 in two weeks and shut down. We now host sellers like it for free.
entry.summary: It answered correctly, charged less than we do, earned $0.18 in two weeks and went offline. Why small x402 sellers fold, and the free hosting we now offer them.

entry.title: Two public records of MCP tool definitions, one day, 23,190 servers: where they agree
entry.summary: HISTOR and heldfast read the same MCP servers a minute apart: 99.1% of 318,389 tools match byte for byte. The rest shows why a digest needs its capture conditions.

entry.title: We built a marketplace for AI agents. Sellers told us the integration wasn't worth it.
entry.summary: Two API sellers declined our federation proposal. Their reasons exposed a cost our protocol didn't account for—and changed what we built next.

entry.title: We Improved WARDEN's Warnings. Twelve Rechecks Changed No Choices.
entry.summary: 720 fresh model answers showed a version-level improvement on six known cases. Twelve Stop rechecks changed no selected IDs. Here is what each result means.

entry.title: A copyable MCP tool-cost check for CI, with passing and failing examples
entry.summary: Pinned commands, the complete snapshot fetcher, and a separate gate for total tokens, descriptions and input schemas.

entry.title: Five Wallets Paid an x402 Seller. What Can We Say About Demand?
entry.summary: A five-wallet audit verifies 24 settlements while separating payment evidence, behavioral signals and unknown customer intent.

entry.title: We Kept WARDEN's 8/10 Thresholds and Fixed Its Credential Index
entry.summary: A reader asked whether shorter secret fragments justified lower thresholds. We compared 6/7/8, reproduced false blocks, and fixed a narrower indexing defect.

entry.title: We rechecked 292 failing MCP packages. 12 newer releases now list tools.
entry.summary: A fresh-install follow-up separates release recovery, optional dependencies and a correction to our own SDK classifier.

entry.title: We attacked our own MCP firewall with its source code open. 14 of 17 attacks got through; now 2 of 23 do
entry.summary: Asked what WARDEN still misses, we wrote 17 attacks on its MCP flow guard with the source open. 14 got through; after the fixes, 2 of 23 do. The rest is named.

entry.title: MCP servers edit the instructions your agent reads. WARDEN 0.18 shows which words changed
entry.summary: In four weeks, 2,345 changes to MCP tool definitions added an "always", "never" or "must" to a description. WARDEN 0.18 shows a re-approval as a word diff.

entry.title: A third of remote MCP servers changed their tool definitions in four weeks. The log is now a dataset.
entry.summary: HISTOR reads every remote MCP registry server daily: in four weeks about a third of them (2,489 of 6,822 hosts) changed their tool list. Open dataset with a DOI.

entry.title: Three x402 sellers compared notes. The routes answer; nobody comes back to buy.
entry.summary: Three x402 sellers compared ledgers: on ours 40,400 unpaid 402s, 23 paid calls from 6 wallets, two of them monitors. What do agents buy twice? So far, nothing.

entry.summary: Every tool definition rides in each model request. We counted 34,374 MCP tool lists: median 1,272 tokens, p90 8,361, 31 packages over 100,000. Check yours free.

entry.summary: A flow guard for MCP tool calls, measured on AgentDojo, and what the 2026-10-18 security audit found after: bypasses, fixes, and what is not yet re-measured.

entry.title: We re-ran our MCP scanner comparison on 14,933 npm and PyPI tool lists, in gVisor, with two more scanners
entry.summary: Five MCP scanners on 14,933 npm/PyPI tool lists and MCPTox's held-out half, in gVisor: WARDEN blocks 171 of 218 poisoned tools, 369 packages; mcp-shield 5,354.

entry.title: We installed 12,915 MCP servers and started each one. 41% never answered.
entry.summary: We installed and started 12,915 MCP servers in a sandbox: 7,656 answered tools/list, 1,239 only with a placeholder key, 5,259 never did. Failure classes by SDK.

entry.title: One key for an agent's tool calls: a prepaid USDC balance on an MCP connection
entry.summary: Paying per call on chain for a $0.001 reading kills adoption: hundreds of MCP clients listed our tools, none paid. /start gives a key topped up in USDC on Base.

entry.title: We tried to buy one call from 100 x402 sellers. Most delivered. Almost nobody is buying.
entry.summary: x402 Bazaar lists 34,768 paid endpoints. We paid 100 sellers for one call: 74 of 85 answered, 4 charged for nothing, 9 failed unpaid. Almost nobody else buys.
